title: Fomo Kernel Behavior Verdict
description: One engine-judged mismatch between what the user said (a closed-vocabulary self-report) and what they did (an engine-owned behavioral metric), frozen so it stays true forever -- including after the thesis row `subject` points at is revised, or the profile label `profile_label_id` names is superseded (#446 cut 1). The readable contract; skills/fomo-kernel/engine/verdicts.py (replay) holds the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency. Stored append-only at <root>/verdicts.jsonl, its own file for the same firewall reason conditions.py:66-72 gives conditions.jsonl: a verdict must never enter problems.check_rules' mechanical reconciliation. Unlike condition-slot.schema.json and condition-check.schema.json, this document has no `input` sub-object: every field is engine-assigned, because an agent that could write its own verdict could record an adjudication nobody made.

rule.description: The rule that judged, and the exact parameter version it judged under. Without this a threshold change makes every prior verdict unrecomputable -- verdicts.RULE_PARAMS is the versioned parameter block this pins to, and verdicts.RULE_PARAM_DIGEST fails the suite the moment a version's parameters change without a new version being added.

subject.description: The *said* half, frozen as both value and row. Value alone cannot be audited; row alone cannot be replayed once a later fold changes what that row resolves to.

store.description: The logical store the row lives in, e.g. "theses" (theses.jsonl).

row_id.description: The specific row's own identity -- a thesis row's event_id, never its stable cross-revision thesis_id. A revision writes a new event_id, so an already-written verdict is never silently repointed at a later restatement.

field.description: The field on that row being judged, e.g. "horizon".

value.description: The frozen value of that field at judgment time. Replay compares against this literal value, never against a fresh read of the row it names.

observed.description: The *done* half, frozen. Behavior is recomputed from the current fold every period, so it drifts unless pinned here.

value.description: e.g. the holding-day count at judgment time.

window.description: The span the observation was measured over.

closed.description: Whether the subject was closed (exited) as of this observation -- horizon_contradiction's own exited axis, frozen the same way as everything else here.

outcome.description: What the rule returned, e.g. "exit_too_fast" or "held_too_long". replay() checks its own recomputation against this.

verdict_source.description: Who judged. "agent" is deliberately absent from this vocabulary until #414 lands: a free-text said-half may be quoted into a question, never adjudicated by the agent alone (references/condition-slots.md gives the same split for condition checks).

date_end.description: The review period this verdict belongs to. One row per (subject, rule, period), the same convention condition-check.schema.json uses.

session_id.description: The session that recorded this verdict. Required so session._append_session_rows can dedupe an idempotent retry of the same finalize -- the same mechanism every other durable store in this codebase already relies on.

profile_label_id.description: Back-reference only, load-bearing for nothing (#446 cut 2, not yet built). Points at an immutable profile-label id, never a line id. Removing this field must not change any replay() result -- replay's signature does not accept it.
